For every integer $n\ge2$, every Boolean function $f$ on $E_n$ invariant under vertex permutations, and every $0<p<1$, $$\label{eq:variance}
 \mathop{\mathrm{Var}}_p(f)\le\frac{2^{17}}{(\log n)^2}I_p(f).$$ No monotonicity assumption is needed.

Let $m\ge2$ be real and let $h:\{0,1\}^J\to\{0,1\}$ satisfy $I_i(h)\le I(h)/m$ for every $i\in J$. If $$k=\frac{\sigma\log m}{64},$$ then $$\label{eq:low-degree}
  \sum_{1\le |S|\le k}\widehat h(S)^2\le m^{-1/4}I(h).$$ Every degree cutoff is interpreted literally for integer degrees $|S|$; in particular, the sum is empty when $k<1$.

Let $3\le m\le n$ be an integer, let $B$ be uniform among the $m$-element subsets of $[n]$, and set $$F_B=\{e\in E_n:e\cap B\ne\varnothing\},
 \qquad k=\frac{\sigma\log m}{64}.$$ Then $$\sum_{S\subseteq E_n}
 \Pr_B\{1\le |S\cap F_B|\le k\}\widehat f(S)^2
 \le \frac{2m}{n}\,m^{-1/4}I(f).
 \label{eq:block-average}$$

Suppose $t=\log n\ge16$, and put $$m=\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor,
 \qquad k=\frac{\sigma\log m}{64}.$$ Then $$\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq E_n\\1\le |S|\le k^2/2}}
       \widehat f(S)^2
 \le 4m^{-1/4}I(f).
 \label{eq:captured-mass}$$

outputs.exact_statement: In this game, there is one globally legal Maker policy that completes an allowed copy of $S$ within at most $21$ actual Maker claims against every legal continuation of Breaker. Equivalently, extend the policy by fresh claims after an earlier win: its Maker set after claim $21$ contains a target whenever the first $20$ Breaker replies are legal.

Let $(A_i,T_i,h_i)$, $1\le i\le r$, be valid claims, where $1\le r<\infty$, and let $p\in\mathbb Z^2$. Define $$\label{eq:combination} T=\{p\}\cup\bigcup_{i=1}^rT_i, \qquad A=\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^r A_i\ \cup\ \bigcap_{i=1}^rT_i\right)\setminus\{p\}, \qquad h=1+\max_i h_i.$$ Then $(A,T,h)$ is valid. Also, at a position with Breaker to move, if $A\cup\{p\}\subseteq M$ and $B\cap T=\varnothing$, then Maker has already won or can win within $h-1$ further Maker moves.

Maker wins the weak Maker–Breaker game within $21$ actual Maker claims on the initially empty $251$-cell board $T_{727}$, and also on the initially empty $17\times17$ board $\{0,\ldots,16\}^2$. In each game, Maker moves first, the players alternate claiming one previously unclaimed cell, and the targets are the allowed copies of $S$ contained in the board.

Suppose it is Maker’s turn at an arbitrary finite position, Maker owns the four cells $$\{(0,0),(1,0),(2,0),(3,0)\},$$ and Breaker owns at most three cells in $$Q=([-3,6]\times[-4,4])\cap\mathbb Z^2.$$ Then Maker has already won or can force a win. Additional Maker cells and arbitrary Breaker cells outside $Q$ are allowed.

Let $(P_j,E_j,h_j)$, $1\leq j\leq m$, be valid reduced cards already placed in one coordinate plane, where $1\leq m<\infty$. Given an attack cell $x$, put $$\label{r25:reduced-rule} \begin{aligned} U&=\bigcup_jP_j,& V&=\bigcup_jE_j,& I&=\bigcap_jE_j,\\ H&=U\cup I,& P&=H\setminus\{x\},& E&=(V\setminus H)\cup\{x\},\qquad h=1+\max_jh_j. \end{aligned}$$ Then $(P,E,h)$ is valid. Its normalization is exactly the full card obtained by Lemma 3 from the normalized children $(P_j,P_j\cup E_j,h_j)$ at $x$; in particular, normalization changes neither the required set nor the height.
